chapter: Life on the road and in the Webb band's book
title: Edgar Sampson's arrangements for Webb
summary: Welburn asks about arrangements; McRae recalls gigging with Chick in 1933-34 and Chick's habit of buying arrangements.

Sampson did a lot -- There was a lot of things that Sampson did. Sampson was one of the most important arrangers. You know, let's talk about Edgar Sampson and the arrangements. When I joined the band in 1936, I always knew -- I knew Chick -- I played a couple of little gigs with him before I joined the band -- before I left town, when I was hanging out with him years ago -- '33-'34--something like that. He was just getting his band together. I think why I had -- I think why I did play a couple of gigs with him, during the summer, Elmer would go to Atlantic City with Claude Hopkins. Remember I was speaking to you -- The band wasn't -- Chick's band wasn't working (inaudible). Elmer would take off and Edgar -- Hilton Jefferson -- the two saxophone players I told you that worked with Claude Hopkins? A little band in Atlantic City? Well Elmer would go to Atlantic City

during those times and work down in Atlantic City. So I would be available to play some gigs with Chick Webb.
And that's when I found out that Chick was spending every nickel he could get hold of for arrangements and things like that.
